texts.preamble: M/S Tampra Homes Pvt. Ltd vs State Of Punjab And Others on 13 December, 2022 In The High Court Of Punjab & Haryana At Chandigarh 109 Cwp-24069-2022 Date of decision: 13.12.2022 M/S Tampra Homes Pvt. Ltd. .........Petitioner Versus State Of Punjab And Others ........Respondents Coram : Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Vinod S. Bhardwaj ***** Present:- Mr. Monty Goyal, Advocate for the petitioner. ***** Vinod S. Bhardwaj, J. (Oral) The instant petition has been filed under Articles 226/227 of the Constitution of India for issuance of a writ in the nature of Mandamus directing the respondents No.1 to 4 to provide police protection to the petitioner and its employees for the execution/performance of his work as per Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 of Government of India read with Food Safety and Standard Rules, 2011.
texts.facts: The instant petition has been filed under Articles 226/227 of the Constitution of India for issuance of a writ in the nature of Mandamus directing the respondents No.1 to 4 to provide police protection to the petitioner and its employees for the execution/performance of his work as per Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 of Government of India read with Food Safety and Standard Rules, 2011.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner contends that the petitioner is a Developer who had set up the colony after taking all necessary statutory approvals alongwith the constructed residential township, the petitioner is also constructed commercial property wherein various multi-national companies are opening their retail outlets including food points. The private respondent, however, is not allowing the restaurants offering non-vegetarian food to be opened in the said locality. 1 of 2 It is contended that the petitioner had submitted their representation to the Director General of Police, Punjab Police Headquarter, Sector-9, Chandigarh against such illegal hardship being created by private respondents but no action has been taken thereupon. He contends that as per his knowledge the aforesaid representation has been marked to the office of the Commissioner of Police, Ludhiana.
texts.petitioner_arguments: Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner contends that the petitioner is a Developer who had set up the colony after taking all necessary statutory approvals alongwith the constructed residential township, the petitioner is also constructed commercial property wherein various multi-national companies are opening their retail outlets including food points. The private respondent, however, is not allowing the restaurants offering non-vegetarian food to be opened in the said locality. 1 of 2 It is contended that the petitioner had submitted their representation to the Director General of Police, Punjab Police Headquarter, Sector-9, Chandigarh against such illegal hardship being created by private respondents but no action has been taken thereupon. He contends that as per his knowledge the aforesaid representation has been marked to the office of the Commissioner of Police, Ludhiana.
